clue.text: High-class daily printed in most attractive capital

indicators.note: printed in means set within the text of another word, so these pieces go inside

parts.note: most attractive means best
U is the old British label for upper-class usage
a daily is a British cleaning woman, also called a char

explanation.surface: A posh newspaper is published in the loveliest city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like a newspaper but is a British cleaning woman; 'printed in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucharest is the capital city of Romania, so capital names it by category.

clue.text: Charlie Parker played this live broadcast's opening work

parts.note: to live is to be, exist

indicators.note: opening means take only the first letter of the following word

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: The jazz saxophonist performed a piece at the start of a live radio show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live broadcast' reads as one phrase, but 'live' is BE and only the first letter of 'broadcast' is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Parker was a pioneer of this fast, complex style of jazz from the 1940s.

clue.text: Poor quality sheep can get butchered at start of spring

indicators.note: butchered means hacked about, so these letters are cut up and rearranged
at start of means take the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Inferior sheep may be slaughtered in early spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get butchered' scrambles SHEEPCAN into CHEAPNES, and the first letter of 'spring' adds the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheapness describes something of low value or shoddy make, the same as poor quality.

clue.text: Woman hesitates to speak, though they take in the workers

indicators.note: to speak means the words are said out loud and the spelling follows their sound

parts.note: a woman can be an aunt, and hesitates can mean teeters, wavers

explanation.surface: A woman hesitates before speaking, even though they welcome workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'workers' is the crossword word for ants, so creatures that take them in, i.e. eat them, are the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: These animals eat ants, and ants are the classic worker insects of crosswords.

clue.text: Current procedure for improving the railways?

definitions.text: Current procedure for improving the railways?

parts.words: Current procedure for improving the railways?
parts.note: the procedure is one that brings electric current to the lines, a modernisation of rail networks

explanation.surface: A present-day method for upgrading train lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'present-day' but means electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: Converting a railway to run on electric power is a standard way of modernising it.

clue.text: When it dawns on us that we've overindulged?

definitions.text: When it dawns on us that we've overindulged?

parts.words: When it dawns on us that we've overindulged?
parts.note: a dawn following a night of excess, when the hangover makes us realise how much we drank

explanation.surface: The moment we realise we have had too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dawns on us' means 'we realise', but literally it is daybreak after a heavy night.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase refers to the hangover felt the next day after heavy drinking.

clue.text: Travel free -but there's a snag!

definitions.meaning: to travel by thumbing lifts, paying nothing
a snag is an unexpected difficulty

explanation.definitionFit: Hitchhiking is free travel, and a problem that holds things up is also called by this word.

clue.text: Henry and possibly Sally's resort

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry and maybe Sally go to a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Aunt Sally is a traditional British pub game where sticks are thrown at a model head, hence an 'aunt' Sally.
explanation.definitionFit: A haunt is a place one often visits, as is a resort in the sense of a regular retreat.

clue.text: Two-wheeled vehicle carrying national leader in flowing garment

indicators.note: in means the letter sits inside the garment's name

parts.note: a toga is the loose robe of ancient Rome

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word it follows

explanation.definitionFit: A tonga is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn cart used in India.

clue.text: Line Hood originally penned before noon in city

clue.text: Express taking soldiers into city centre, ultimately

clue.text: Astronomical phenomenon largely affecting horse and bullock

clue.text: Browning's young girl in a spot with Dad

clue.text: Cultivated swimmers are spotted here

clue.text: What could be a knight's fantasy, perhaps

clue.text: Ring doctor by street nearest the centre

clue.text: Maybe 18's old message is possible to cancel

clue.text: Big box carried by odd Scottish players

clue.text: Cleric caught entering through door at rear
